items.prompt:
If an object's kinetic energy increases, energy was transferred:
A) Away from it
B) To it
C) Nowhere
D) Into color

steps: Gaining kinetic energy means energy was transferred to the object.

items.prompt:
If an object slows down, its kinetic energy was transferred:
A) To it
B) Away from it
C) Created
D) Destroyed

steps: Slowing means kinetic energy was transferred away.

items.prompt:
Energy can be:
A) Created from nothing
B) Destroyed completely
C) Only transferred, not created or destroyed
D) Made by friction
items.answer: C) Only transferred, not created or destroyed

steps: Energy is conserved; it is only transferred.

items.prompt:
A rolling ball slows and stops on a rough floor. Its kinetic energy became:
A) More motion
B) Heat from friction
C) Light
D) Sound only, with no heat

steps: Friction converts the motion energy into heat.

items.prompt:
A player kicks a still ball and it speeds off. The energy came from:
A) Nowhere
B) The player's kick
C) The ground
D) The air ahead

steps: The kick transferred energy to the ball.

items.prompt:
A car brakes and slows. Its kinetic energy is mostly transferred to:
A) More speed
B) Heat in the brakes
C) The color of the car
D) The radio

steps: Braking turns kinetic energy into heat in the brakes.

items.prompt:
Why is a change in an object's kinetic energy evidence of an energy transfer?
A) Energy appears randomly
B) Energy is conserved, so a change must come from a transfer
C) Kinetic energy is not energy
D) Energy can be destroyed
items.answer: B) Energy is conserved, so a change must come from a transfer

steps: Since energy is conserved, any change in kinetic energy reflects a transfer.

items.prompt:
A sled on smooth ice barely slows down. The best reason is:
A) Ice adds energy
B) Little friction means little energy is transferred away
C) The sled has no kinetic energy
D) Energy was destroyed
items.answer: B) Little friction means little energy is transferred away

steps: Low friction means little kinetic energy is transferred away.
